- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below true outcome, reduce forecast bias downward by 2–5% to avoid underestimating bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above true outcome, adjust upward by 2–5% to correct for pessimism-induced overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp spike (≥5% from prior 3-day average) and forecast lags by 2+ days, add 1–3 days of lagged momentum to forecast.  
- After a forecast spike (≥10% above mean), reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot and align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.1 or vice versa), adjust forecast horizon to 10–15 days shorter to reflect sentiment volatility.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, apply a smoothing filter to reduce noise and avoid overfitting to recent extremes.
